Our philosophy

Consistency beats intensity.

Gym Headz exists to help people lose body fat, build muscle and get stronger, without guesswork. We focus on progressive training, sensible nutrition and recovery that you can sustain for years, not weeks.

Whether you are starting your first month or preparing for a competition, you train with a plan, track your progress and adjust as you go.

How we train

  • Progressive overload: small, measured increases in load or reps over time
  • Technique first: form before weight, every session
  • Recovery counts: sleep, rest days and deloads are part of the plan
  • Honest tracking: your data decides the next step, not hype

Meet the owner

Sipho Mazibuko

Sipho Mazibuko is the CEO, Gym Owner and coach at Gym Headz.

He built Gym Headz as a serious, no-nonsense place to train. As a coach, he works with clients one-on-one on losing weight and building muscle, using a personal training plan, nutrition guidance and recovery, and adjusting it as results come in.

What Sipho coaches

  • Losing body fat while keeping strength and muscle
  • Building muscle with progressive training and sensible nutrition

Training programmes

Programmes for every level.

Each programme lists its goal, experience level, duration, equipment, sets, reps, rest periods and warm-up. Modifications are included for every exercise.

Fat loss · Beginner

Full-Body Foundations

Three sessions a week built around squats, presses, rows and hinges, with a short conditioning finish.

  • Goblet squat 3 × 10–12
  • Dumbbell row 3 × 10–12
  • Incline push-up 3 × 8–12
  • Farmer carry 3 × 40 m
45 minDumbbells, bench
Muscle · Intermediate

Upper / Lower Hypertrophy

Four sessions a week with moderate loads, controlled tempo and progressive overload tracked session to session.

  • Barbell bench press 4 × 6–10
  • Romanian deadlift 3 × 8–10
  • Lat pulldown 3 × 10–12
  • Leg press 3 × 10–15
60 minFull gym
Strength · Advanced

Strength Foundations

Heavy compound lifts on a four-day split, with technique checkpoints and planned deload weeks.

  • Back squat 5 × 3–5
  • Deadlift 3 × 3–5
  • Overhead press 4 × 4–6
  • Pull-up 3 × max-minus-2
75 minBarbell, rack

Sample programmes are guidance only. Exact plans are set with your coach and adjusted to your experience, injuries and schedule.

Nutrition & energy

Calories, protein and recovery.

Your body weight changes when energy intake sits above or below what you burn. Protein supports muscle repair, and training gives the signal for muscle to grow. Use the estimator below as a starting point, then adjust using your weekly progress.

Fat loss

A moderate deficit of roughly 15–20% can support gradual fat loss while resistance training and adequate protein help preserve muscle.

Muscle building

A modest surplus of about 5–10% above maintenance, paired with progressive training, may support lean mass gain.

Body recomposition

Some people gain muscle while losing fat near maintenance calories, especially when returning to training or training consistently.

Daily calorie estimator

Your estimate

Enter your details to see your estimated maintenance calories, goal range, protein target and a sample meal structure.

These are general estimates based on the Mifflin–St Jeor equation and self-reported activity. They are not a medical prescription. Speak to a doctor or registered dietitian before major dietary changes, especially if you have a medical condition.

Affordable South African staples

  • Eggs, oats and plain yoghurt
  • Chicken, lean beef and tinned fish
  • Beans, lentils and brown rice
  • Maize meal, potatoes and seasonal vegetables
  • Fruit and milk

Simple plate method

  • Half the plate: vegetables or fruit
  • A quarter: protein at each meal
  • A quarter: carbohydrates around training
  • A thumb-sized portion of fat from oils, nuts or avocado

Set your preferences

Dietary restrictions, allergies and food dislikes can be edited with your coach or in your member profile once accounts are enabled.

Frequently asked

Do I need experience to join?

No. Programmes are grouped by beginner, intermediate and advanced, and every exercise has modifications.

Can I train on a rest day?

Light mobility and a walk are encouraged. Heavy sessions should follow your programme's recovery guidance.

Will I lose fat and gain muscle at the same time?

It depends on training history, nutrition and recovery. Results vary, and no outcome is guaranteed.
